hello.note: Reply: وعليكم السلام (w 'alaikum is-salaam). Casual: هلا (hala) or مرحبا (marhaba).

goodbye.note: Also very Gulf: في أمان الله (fi amaan illah), 'in God's safekeeping'.

please.note: To a woman: من فضلج (min fadhlich). In everyday Gulf requests لو سمحت (law samaht) is more common.

thank_you.note: To a woman: مشكورة (mashkoora). Also: شكرا (shukran), تسلم (tislam).

yes.note: Emiratis also say هيه (heeh). Formal: نعم (na'am).

sorry.note: A woman says: آسفة (aasfa). Very Emirati: السموحة (is-smooha).

excuse_me.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti). Very polite Gulf: طال عمرك (taal 'umrak).

how_are_you.note: To a woman: شحالج؟ (sh-haalich?). Elsewhere in the Gulf: شلونك؟ (shlonak?)

im_fine.note: Lit. 'well, God keep you safe', the usual thanks. To a woman: الله يسلمج (allah ysalmich).

whats_your_name.note: To a woman: شو اسمج؟ (shu ismich?). Extra polite: شو الاسم الكريم؟ (shu il-ism il-kareem?)

where_from.note: To a woman: إنتي من وين؟ (inti min wain?)

speak_english.note: To a woman: تتكلمين إنجليزي؟ (titkallameen ingleezi?)

dont_understand.note: Lit. 'I didn't understand'. Emirati also: مب فاهم (mob faahim); a woman says مب فاهمة (mob faahma).

speak_slowly.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي، تكلمي شوي شوي (law samahti, tkallami shwai shwai).

what.note: Elsewhere in the Gulf: شنو؟ (shinu?) or وش؟ (wish?). Polite 'pardon?': نعم؟ (na'am?)

how_much.note: Often pronounced bcham in the Emirates.

where_bathroom.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

can_you_help.note: To a woman: ممكن تساعديني؟ (mumkin tsaa'ideeni?)

water.note: The everyday Gulf word; formal ماء (maa) is understood too.

coffee.note: In the Gulf this usually means Arabic coffee with cardamom, served in small cups.

tea.note: Many Gulf speakers say chaay. Local favourite: كرك (karak), strong spiced milk tea.

bread.note: Careful: عيش ('aish) means rice in the Gulf, not bread.

im_hungry.note: A woman says: أنا جوعانة (ana joo'aana). Many Emiratis say يوعان (yoo'aan).

menu_please.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

bill_please.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

delicious.note: Also: وايد حلو (waayed hilu), 'really good'. Very Gulf: بنين (bneen).

no_meat.note: Vegetarian: نباتي (nabaati); a woman says نباتية (nabaatiyya).

left.note: To a driver: لف يسار (liff yisaar), 'turn left'.

right.note: To a driver: لف يمين (liff yimeen), 'turn right'.

straight_ahead.note: The everyday Gulf word; you'll also hear على طول ('ala tool).

stop_here.note: To a woman: وقفي هني لو سمحتي (waggfi hni law samahti). Also: نزلني هني (nazzilni hni), 'drop me here'.

hotel.note: The ق is said as g in the Gulf: fundug, not funduq.

train_station.note: In Dubai you'll more often want محطة المترو (mahattat il-metro), the metro station.

want_to_go.note: To a taxi: ودني … (waddni …), 'take me to …'. Elsewhere in the Gulf: أبي / أبغى (abi / abgha).

one_ticket.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti). Also common: تكت (tikit).

too_expensive.note: وايد (waayed), 'very, a lot', is a key Gulf word.

cheaper.note: Plural 'you', addressing the shop, so it suits any assistant.

id_like_this.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti). Also: بآخذ هذا (baakhidh hadha), 'I'll take this'.

just_looking.note: Also: بس أشوف (bas ashoof). Add مشكور (mashkoor) to thank them.

pay_card.note: Shops often ask: كاش ولا كارد؟ (kaash walla kaard?), 'cash or card?'

big.note: Often pronounced chbeer in the Emirates.

tomorrow.note: Also heard: بكرة (bukra), from other Arabic dialects.

yesterday.note: البارحة (il-baarha) is last night, and often just yesterday.

good_night.note: To a woman: تصبحين على خير (tisbaheen 'ala khair). Reply: وإنت من أهله (w inta min ahla).

see_you_later.note: To a woman: أشوفج بعدين (ashoofich ba'dain).

wait_moment.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti). Casual: اصبر شوي (isbir shwai), 'hang on a bit'.

call_police.note: To a woman: اتصلي بالشرطة! (ittasli bish-shurta!). UAE police emergency: 999.

need_doctor.note: A woman says: محتاجة دكتور (mihtaaja diktoor).

im_lost.note: A woman says: أنا ضايعة (ana dhaay'a). Also: ضعت (dhi't), 'I got lost'.

dont_feel_well.note: Also: أنا مريض (ana mareedh), 'I'm ill'; a woman says مريضة (mareedha).

be_careful.note: To a woman: انتبهي! (intibhi!). Also: دير بالك! (deer baalak!)

no_problem.note: Very Gulf: ما عليه (ma 'alaih), 'never mind, it's fine'.

of_course.note: Agreeing to a request, Gulf speakers say أبشر (abshir); to a woman أبشري (abshiri).

dont_know.note: The Gulf way to say it; ما أعرف (ma a'rif) is also used.

dont_like_it.note: مب (mob) is the Emirati 'not'; elsewhere in the Gulf: مو عاجبني (mu 'aajibni).

im_tired.note: A woman says: أنا تعبانة (ana ta'baana). In the Gulf تعبان can also mean unwell.

im_happy.note: A woman says: أنا مستانسة (ana mistaansa). Also: فرحان (farhaan).

welcome.note: To a woman: حياج الله (hayyaach allah). Also: أهلا وسهلا (ahlan wa sahlan).

congratulations.note: Reply: الله يبارك فيك (allah ybaarik feek).
